title: Splitting & Filtering Strings
description: Test your understanding of breaking strings apart with .split(), the .split('') quirk, and filtering unwanted characters out of an array with Array.filter().

questions.question: What does `'3 + 9'.split(' ')` do?
options: It returns the exact same string unchanged
It breaks the string into an array of pieces wherever a space appears, giving ['3', '+', '9']
It deletes all spaces and joins the string back together
It converts the string into a single number
questions.explanation: `.split(' ')` breaks a string apart everywhere a space occurs, turning '3 + 9' into the array ['3', '+', '9'].

questions.question: Why does `'3 +9'.split(' ')` fail to correctly parse the expression?
options: Because .split() cannot be used on strings containing numbers
Because it throws a runtime error when a plus sign is present
Because with no space between '+' and '9', they aren't split apart, so one array element ends up as "+9" instead of separate "+" and "9"
Because .split(' ') only works on strings longer than five characters
questions.explanation: Since .split(' ') only breaks on spaces, a missing space means '+' and '9' stay glued together as one array element.

questions.question: What does `.split('')` (an empty string argument) do to a string?
options: It separates every single character into its own element in the resulting array
It splits the string only at whitespace characters
It returns the string unchanged, wrapped in an array
It removes all punctuation from the string
questions.explanation: Passing an empty string to .split() is the JavaScript quirk the article highlights: it separates every individual character into its own array element.

questions.question: After running `'3 +9'.split('')`, what unwanted element ends up in the resulting array?
options: The character '+'
The character '9'
An empty string ('')
A whitespace character (' ')
questions.explanation: Splitting on every character also captures the space itself as its own element, which then needs to be filtered out.

questions.question: What is the general purpose of `Array.filter()`?
options: It sorts every element in an array from smallest to largest
It goes through each element and keeps only the ones that satisfy a given condition, removing the rest
It permanently converts an array into a string
It adds new elements to the end of an array
questions.explanation: `Array.filter()` checks every element against a condition function and builds a new array containing only the elements that pass.

questions.question: In the condition `char != ' '`, what does the `!=` operator mean?
options: 'is exactly equal to'
'is greater than'
'is not equal to'
'assigns a new value to'
questions.explanation: `!=` is the 'not equal to' operator, so `char != ' '` asks whether char is anything other than a space.

questions.question: What does `Array.filter()` do with an element when its condition function returns `false` for that element?
options: It removes that element from the resulting array
It duplicates that element in the resulting array
It converts that element to `null` but keeps its position
It stops the filtering process entirely
questions.explanation: When the condition evaluates to false for a given element, .filter() excludes it from the array it returns.

questions.question: In `splitted.filter(char => char != ' ')`, what does `char` represent as `.filter()` runs?
options: The very first character of the original string only
The name of the array itself
A fixed value equal to a space
Each individual element of the array, one at a time, as filter checks it against the condition
questions.explanation: `char` is the parameter name for whichever array element .filter() is currently testing against the condition.

questions.question: According to the article, why does the author encourage reading documentation like MDN, even while calling it 'boring'?
options: Because documentation is required before any code will run
Because reading documentation is a core skill every programmer should build, even when it isn't exciting
Because MDN docs contain the only correct version of JavaScript
Because without it, .filter() and .split() won't function
questions.explanation: The article frames reading documentation as one of the essential skills every programmer should have, regardless of how tedious it feels.

questions.question: Given `const char = '3'; const condition = char != ' '`, what does `condition` evaluate to?
options: false, since '3' is a whitespace character
undefined, since strings cannot be compared this way
true, since '3' is not equal to the space character
'3', since the comparison returns the value itself
questions.explanation: '3' is not the same as ' ', so the != comparison evaluates to true.
